topStories.headline: November Storm Knocks Out West Portal Muni Station, Floods Swath of San Francisco
topStories.dek: Wednesday's record-breaking deluge left the West Portal Muni station with reported issues and swamped streets across the city.
topStories.body:
A powerful storm on Wednesday, November 18 dumped more than two inches of rain on downtown San Francisco in a matter of hours, triggering what officials described as a record number of 911 calls and causing widespread flooding, downed trees, and dislocated manhole covers across the city.

For riders on the K Ingleside, M Ocean View, and L Taraval lines, the storm hit close to home. Viktoriya Wise, streets director for the San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency, confirmed that West Portal station was facing issues during the storm. The hub is a critical bottleneck for Muni Metro trains in all directions, and any disruption there cascades quickly across the westside network.

The Public Utilities Commission general manager Dennis Herrera noted at a briefing that some flooding occurred in areas not normally considered flood-prone, attributing the unusual pattern to the sheer volume of rain falling in a very short time. Muni's Van Ness station also temporarily closed before reopening, while BART, SamTrans, and Golden Gate Ferry all reported delays or cancellations during the storm.

As of publication, SFMTA had not released a full post-incident summary for November 18. Riders should check sfmta.com for service updates before traveling through West Portal station in the days ahead.

topStories.headline: CSU Faculty Strike Vote Closes as Union Takes Demands to Board of Trustees
topStories.dek: California Faculty Association members finished their strike authorization ballot this week even as hundreds rallied outside the CSU Board of Trustees meeting in Long Beach.
topStories.body:
The strike threat looming over San Francisco State University and the broader California State University system sharpened dramatically this week. Faculty and staff staged a rally outside the CSU Board of Trustees meeting on Tuesday, November 17 in Long Beach, demanding better pay and benefits as two unions pushed for new agreements.

The California Faculty Association — which represents 29,000 professors, lecturers, librarians, counselors, and coaches across the CSU's 23 campuses — has been voting on whether to authorize a strike after more than 18 months of stalled contract negotiations. The union declared impasse over the summer after rejecting CSU's offer of a one-time three-percent raise. Beyond wages, faculty are seeking stronger job protections for temporary lecturers, limits on workload, guardrails on artificial intelligence use, and broader academic freedom safeguards.

A 'yes' vote does not automatically trigger a walkout. Union leaders have said they would decide if and when to strike after the mediation and fact-finding process concludes. CSU officials say they remain committed to bargaining in good faith and have already reached tentative agreements with five or six other campus bargaining units representing tens of thousands of employees.

At SFSU, faculty and students have been bracing for a possible strike since the fact-finding hearings held earlier this month. The Golden Gate Xpress reported that SFSU's CFA chapter described recent negotiations as a 'slog,' and that the student union has pledged to support faculty if a walkout is called. The last CFA strike lasted one day in January 2024 before a deal was reached.

topStories.headline: SFSU's Spring 2027 Admits Must Accept Offers by December 1
topStories.dek: The university is urging prospective spring students to confirm enrollment as SFSU rides its first enrollment increase in more than a decade.
topStories.body:
San Francisco State University posted a reminder on November 18 that students admitted for Spring 2027 must accept their enrollment offers by December 1. The deadline applies to incoming freshmen, transfer students, and graduate applicants who received admission decisions for the spring term.

The notice arrives at a moment of unusual momentum for SFSU. The university reported in October that its fall 2026 incoming student enrollment was up 18 percent compared to the previous year, including a 20 percent lift in new undergraduate enrollment — the first year-over-year increase in more than a decade. University President Lynn Mahoney credited years of focused work to strengthen recruitment and improve the experience of prospective students.

Prospective students can accept their offers through the SFSU Student Center at sfsu.edu. The university notes that spring admission is a less common entry point but can offer a less competitive path into some programs. Any student who misses the December 1 deadline risks forfeiting their spot.

moreNews.headline: Board of Supervisors Unanimously Approves Stonestown Redevelopment Plan
moreNews.body: The San Francisco Board of Supervisors voted unanimously to approve Brookfield Properties' sweeping plan to develop 30 acres of new housing, parks, and retail around Stonestown Galleria and Lake Merced — one of the largest residential projects approved in the city in five decades. The plan calls for 3,500 residential units, 20 percent of which will be affordable, plus 200 senior housing units, 6 acres of new parks, and a new Main Street with roughly 150,000 square feet of retail along 20th Avenue, while keeping the existing mall intact. The vote was reported by Bisnow in late July 2026. No construction timeline has been announced.

moreNews.headline: SFSU Dietetics Students Win Scholarships
moreNews.body: San Francisco State University announced on November 18 that students in its dietetics program had won scholarships, according to a posting on the university's news site. No additional details about the scholarship amounts, donors, or number of recipients were immediately available from the SFSU news listing; the full story was listed as forthcoming on sfsu.edu.
